answer.answer:
Three firms recur across more than one jointly developed machine in the material to hand: Firm_060 appears on three, and Firm_061 and Firm_082 on two each, with Firm_061 pairing with Firm_060 twice and Firm_082 pairing with a different partner each time. Everyone else named appears only once, including the large seven-firm and five-firm consortia. These are census records of deployed machines rather than a full partnership register, so the counts describe the retrieved set and not the whole record, and the graph carries them as manufacturer, distributor and developer roles rather than as a "co-development" relation of its own.

**Firm_060, three records.** It is the most recurrent partner in this set. In census_RXM6-4, Firm_168, Firm_060, Firm_008, Firm_009 and Firm_064 jointly developed a construction robot [1]; the edges split those roles, with Firm_168, Firm_060 and Firm_008 as manufacturers and Firm_009 and Firm_064 as distributors, and this is the one record in the set tied to a process record, census_RXM6-4 being the census record of RP14. In census_RXM6-7, Firm_060 worked with Firm_061 and Firm_079 [2], a steel-working machine. In census_RXM6-6, Firm_060 worked with Firm_061 alone [3], again on steel.

**Firm_061, two records.** Both of its appearances are alongside Firm_060 (census_RXM6-7 and census_RXM6-6), so the pairing, not just the firm, repeats.

**Firm_082, two records, two different partners.** In census_RXM8-3 it partnered with Firm_072 [4], and in census_RXM8-1 with Firm_003 [5]. That is a different pattern from the Firm_060/Firm_061 pairing: a recurring developer rotating collaborators.

**Single-appearance partnerships in this set.** census_RXM23-5 was developed by a seven-firm group: Firm_177, Firm_002, Firm_018, Firm_068, Firm_094, Firm_134 and Firm_209 [6]. census_RXH8-2 pairs Firm_097 and Firm_098 [7] on a timber machine. census_RXH5-4 names Firm_027, Firm_028 and Firm_033 [8], and is the only record here where the graph uses a developedBy edge rather than hasManufacturer.

**What this does not establish.** None of these census records carries an enabler activation, a readiness level or a firm-level count in the material retrieved, so no claim can be made about which capabilities these collaborations exercise, and a firm absent from this list may well appear in records outside it. If you need a defensible ranking of repeat collaborators, it should be built from a lookup over all census records with their manufacturer and developer edges, not from this selection.
